commentary: Sweden's spring 2026 legislative agenda unfolds against a challenging economic backdrop: GDP growth of just 0.82% in 2024 — far below Denmark's 3.48% and Norway's 2.10% — while unemployment has risen to 8.69% in 2025, the highest rate since 2021. The government's triple-budget submission (Spring Economic Proposition HD03100, supplementary budget HD0399, and extra budget HD03236) represents a coordinated fiscal response, with the fuel tax cut and energy support in HD03236 providing direct household relief at a cost to climate commitments. Inflation has retreated sharply from its 2023 peak of 8.55% to 2.84% in 2024, reducing the Riksbank's constraint on fiscal stimulus, but structural unemployment above 8.5% remains the central economic challenge as Sweden heads toward its September 2026 election.
